newsitem.title: UK: Zinc again soars on LME, approaches $1,500.
newsitem.headline: Zinc again soars on LME, approaches $1,500.

text.p: Zinc prices extended their vigorous rally in Thursday LME pre-market trading, hitting a new 6-3/4 year high of $1,495.
Other metals markets were steadier, which reflected the mark-up late on Wednesday and strength in copper post-option declarations.
But it was zinc that dominated the picture, with the market now some $150 up from the levels prevailing little more than a week ago.
Traders said the combination of speculative fund buying and burgeoning tightness with major shorts finding stocks tightly-held was keeping the market on an upward tack.
Although $1,500 is a psychological level, the chart target is around $1,520/30, they said.
Recent business was at $1,490 a tonne, up $27 from Wednesday's kerb close. The cash/threes contango was a slightly wider $6/8.
Analysts said the dizzy rise in prices had left the market overextended on the charts.
"The market is overbought, but if it is looking technically tight it could go higher," William Adams of LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.

Copper was trading nearer the higher end of the $$2,405/15 range reached late on Wednesday. Three months was at $2,415, up $25 from the previous kerb, while the spread was at a $150/157 backwardation.
Traders said July tightness would continue unabated in the short-term, with little sign of an influx of stocks being attracted by high spot prices.
Aluminium was trading at $1,617, up $7, although the market reached this level during inter-office trade on Wednesday night.
Traders see aluminium making slow but steady progress, against a background of falling stocks.
Lead followed zinc, and was $7 higher at $639, while nickel was $30 up at $6,970. Tin gained just $5 at $5,540, and alloy was quoted at a steadier $1,460/70.
